status: proposal. Every value marked (J) is the planner's or the team's judgement. Nothing here is a measurement of a real phone or a real person. The arcminute minimum and every viewport figure are UNVERIFIED.
unverified: the arcminute minimum (the planner recalls the ISO 9241-3 range of roughly 16 to 22 arcminutes for character height but did not re-read it; 18 and 21 come from the research note's 0.30 and 0.35 degree floor and target for a 50+ viewer)
every viewport figure below: they describe typical phones from published diagonal and pixel counts, not a measured handset
how a given player implements fill or zoom: the 10% crop of fill_20x9 is arithmetic for a 20:9 screen, not a measurement of any app
the device scaler: a phone's own scaler is not knowable here; bicubic is an assumption (the research brackets six scalers)
messenger transcode rules: the shared scenario imitates 'a messenger' (480p, about 1 Mbps, veryfast); it is not WhatsApp's or any service's encoder
the viewing distance for video (35 cm is the research note's design distance for text, 40 cm its 50+ margin)

distance_cm.source: research/mobile-delivery.md Q3: smartphone text is held at a mean of 36.2 cm for messages and 32.2 cm for web pages (Bababekova et al. 2011, abstract via a search digest); 35 cm is the design distance and 40 cm the 50+ margin (J). The verdict is taken at the 'verdict' distance and the 40 cm figure is written next to it.
distance_cm.proxy_note: playbooks/mobile-delivery.md Exercise 4 reads the captions at 35 cm and then at 50 cm as a proxy for a 50+ viewer. 50 cm is reported (INFO) and never gates; the maker's phone test question 3 is the measurement.

x_height.applies_to: the x-height of the Latin caption face (probe 'x'); for an Indic script the height of the dominant band from the top of the headline to the baseline stands in for the height of the base letter (W-18 sizes Gujarati by the height of KA), which is an analogue, not the same thing
x_height.source: floor_pct and target_pct: DECISIONS.md W-63 and research/mobile-delivery.md T-M2 (must-read type x-height 3.2% hard floor, 3.8% target of picture height, which research computes as 0.30 and 0.35 degrees at 40 cm on a 6.1 in landscape-fit screen). floor_arcmin 18 = 0.30 degrees and target_arcmin 21 = 0.35 degrees (J; the same angles taken at the verdict distance).

contrast.formula: WCAG 2.1 relative luminance of the decoded sRGB pixels: (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05); the fill is the 98th percentile of luminance inside the caption box, the outline is the 2nd percentile
contrast.source: WCAG AA (4.5:1) and AAA (7:1); research/mobile-delivery.md T-M2 contrast 4.5:1, 7:1 target

stroke.source: research/mobile-delivery.md Q3 and T-M2: meaning-bearing strokes 4 px, decoration 3 px, no 1 px lines; through a 360p proxy a 3 px line keeps 0.61 and a 4 px line 0.84. min_effective_px is the stroke width after the scenario's smallest grid (the device grid, or the 480p share grid for 'shared'); retention_min is the contrast a line keeps after the same step. Lines of must_survive_from_width_px or more are gated; thinner lines are measured and reported.

box90.source: W-18: captions inside the 90% by 90% box; ROADMAP section 6

position.source: DECISIONS.md W-63 (text box 5 to 95% across, 12 to 88% down; a 20:9 phone in fill crops 9 to 10% top and bottom) and reviews/04-hindu-mobile-briefs-review.md Part 0.2. The 88% limit is the 90% crop line with a 2-point margin; it is also used when --aspect 19.5:9 moves the crop line to about 91%, which keeps the stricter figure.

title.measured_as: the ink height of the title line (top of the tallest letter to the baseline) as a percentage of picture height
title.source: ROADMAP.md section 6 (type at 5% of picture height); read here as ink height, which is stricter than a font-size reading (UNVERIFIED reading)

marks.source: build plan WP-08: at least 2 px of ink in the mark's zone after the downscale to each scenario; the zone is derived by differential rendering at 8x with and without the mark's codepoints (no coordinate stored); zone_iou_min is a guard added here so that another letter's ink landing in the zone does not count as the mark

iou.source: build plan WP-08: libass ink against a Pillow-raqm reference rendering, at least 0.9, or a shaping finding for that script

degrade_shared.source: build plan WP-08: re-encoded to 480p at about 1 Mbps with veryfast to imitate a messenger (J)

portrait.description: phone held upright, picture full width in a player or chat (the 'degraded by design' view of the research, K3)
portrait.gate_reason: upright viewing is degraded by design: no caption that fits the 90% box reaches the x-height floor on a 36 mm tall picture; the hand-over says 'turn it sideways'
portrait.source: 6.1 in 19.5:9 class, 390x844 CSS px at device pixel ratio 3 (J)

landscape.description: the same phone held sideways, 16:9 picture fitted to the height (bars at the sides): the intended view
landscape.source: 6.1 in 19.5:9 class, 844x390 CSS px at device pixel ratio 3 (J)

small_portrait.description: a small upright phone, picture full width
small_portrait.source: a 6.5 in 720x1600 class phone (Redmi 9A class, 360x800 CSS px at ratio 2; research/mobile-delivery.md Q-F4) (J)

shared.description: the file after a messenger's recompression (480p, about 1 Mbps, veryfast), viewed sideways
shared.gate_reason: what a relative actually receives if a copy is forwarded
shared.source: as landscape, plus the degrade_shared step (J)

fill_20x9.description: a 20:9 phone held sideways with the player set to fill or zoom: the picture is scaled to the screen width, so it is 11.25 units tall on a 9-unit screen and about 10% of the picture height is cropped at the top and at the bottom
fill_20x9.gate_reason: a viewer can tap fill on any player

file_check.source: the file's own burned lines (decoded, differenced against a caption-free frame, H.264 CRF 20) against the clean libass drawing of the same ASS; 0.8 tolerates the encoder's softening of thin strokes (J)
